titre: UK Politician Downplays Fears Around GTA 6 Content For Kids, Says She's More Concerned About The Amount of Time They'll Likely Play It
chapo: Prominent U.K. politician Kemi Badenoch has downplayed parents' fears over the violent content found in GTA 6, and said she's more concerned by how long many kids will likely spend in their bedrooms playing it.
extrait: Prominent U.K. politician Kemi Badenoch has downplayed parents' fears over the violent content found in GTA 6, and said that she's more concerned by how long many kids will likely spend in their bedrooms playing it. It's perhaps a surprising stance from Badenoch as leader of the right-leaning Conservative party, though one that she said was informed by her own experiences with video games while younger. "I would be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically," Badenoch said during a news conference today broadcast via Sky News. "I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter — I didn't hit anybody after playing those games. "I haven't played Grand Theft Auto, I know people are worried about the game content," Badenoch continued. "At the same time, I'd be more worried about a kid who played it all day, who was in their bedroom all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went outside to do something else." The subject of GTA 6 arose as the Tory leader laid out more of her party's education policy, which calls for a cut in the amount of time children spend in front of screens while at school. Indeed, Badenoch announced that funds would be diverted from the U.K. government's school laptop budget to buy millions of physical textbooks instead. GTA 6 is now just days away from launch and we have a pretty good idea of the adult content that will be on offer in Rockstar's blockbuster. Age ratings from around the world describe GTA 6 as living up to its usual expectations, with the ESRB in particular warning that the game features "blood and gore, intense violence, mature humor, nudity, strong language, strong sexual content and use of drugs and alcohol." While GTA 6 is of course rated for adults only, it's fair to say that it's likely that millions of under 18s will end up playing it anyway, if indeed they haven't already begun forging their school sick notes in order to do so. Rather than pretend no kids will play it, Badenoch is perhaps simply trying to draw something of a compromise. Of course some younger fans will likely play GTA 6 — but no one should be mainlining it 24/7 in their bedroom, full stop. GTA 6 launches for PlayStation 5 and Xbox Series X/S November 19. For more, you can check out IGN's preview from earlier this year. The UK's Conservative Party leader, Kemi Badenoch, has spoken out about GTA 6 and the inevitable, apparently timeless concerns about video games causing violence, saying she's less worried about that than about children not touching grass. Speaking in a news conference today (via Sky News), Badenoch is asked about how she'd convince parents to reduce screen time for children playing GTA 6, and if she has any concern about "the impact [it] might have on young boys when during the game you might have to shoot civilians and so on." The Tory leader has more concern about one of these things than the other. "I think I'd be more worried about the amount of time people were spending on a game than the game specifically," she begins. "I remember in my childhood playing Mortal Kombat and Street Fighter – I didn't hit anybody after playing those games. "I haven't played Grand Theft Auto," she continues, while acknowledging that "I know people are worried about the game content." Badenoch adds: "I'd be more worried about a kid who is in their bedroom all day, who played it all day, than one who spends half an hour on it and then went out and did something else." Gamers have been dealing with the suggestion that games can inspire violence for decades now, and it's little wonder that GTA 6 is bringing that conversation back up in one form or another. Before Miami-Dade's slew of real-life marketing kicked off earlier this year, Republican Miami-Dade County commissioner Juan Carlos Bermudez and Sheriff Rosie Cordero-Stutz both spoke out against the concept, with Bermudez saying that "we should be promoting the Miami-Dade we have worked so hard to build, not a fictional version of our community defined by crime and violence." He said he was "not against video games, but to go out and get a video game where – which glorifies not only our first responders getting shot, but also pedestrians and residents – it's nonsensical." Anyway, since then, a $1 million billboard went up in Miami, and the Miami Heat is being turned into the Vice City Heat for a special game this week, so that argument clearly wasn't particularly effective.
